From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 18 Jul 2027 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Security kickoff + pen test request & vuln SLA for BrightPath Health

Hi Maya, Daniel —

Great to meet today — thanks for walking us through BrightPath’s data flow and use cases. Quick recap and proposed next steps from our side so we keep momentum for the pilot procurement:  

- Ask: we’ll need a recent penetration test report (most recent 12 months preferred) and confirmation of BrightPath’s SOC 2 scope (Type II report or AOC). If you don’t have a public AOC, a redacted copy is fine.
- Vendor options: you can either share your internal PT report or we can coordinate a vendor-run engagement (we frequently work with Cobalt and a couple of other partners).
- Vulnerability management: standard handback SLA we recommend is 30 days for critical fixes (we can extend to 45 on constrained environments); cadence for authenticated scans we typically recommend quarterly with high-frequency quick scans for public endpoints.
- Disclosure: we ask customers to notify us within 48 hours of any regulatory-impacting incidents; we’ll provide a contact list and triage workflow.

Attached: BP_pentest_scope_template.pdf (blank scope you can fill), redwood_vuln_sla_v1.xlsx (example SLA and remediation tiers).

Next concrete steps: could you 1) confirm whether you’ll share an internal PT report or want Redwood to run/coordinate one, and 2) send the vendor security questionnaire (if you have one) or a list of higher-risk assets to include in scope?

I’m happy to do a vendor-kickoff call with your security lead + our security engineer (Ben) next week — what windows work for you on Tue/Wed?

Thanks,

Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Direct: +1 (415) 555-0192

Subject: Re: Security kickoff + pen test request & vuln SLA for BrightPath Health

Jordan — thanks, and likewise — good call. A few quick clarifications from our security team so we can move fast: 

1) SOC 2: BrightPath completed SOC 2 Type II in 2026; we have an AOC but will need to redact customer names. That should be fine — will attach by EOD.
2) HIPAA/GDPR: we are HIPAA-covered; we also have a DPA for EU data but our pilot will only include US PHI. Please confirm Redwood’s handling for PHI in the hosted environment (we asked during the demo but want written confirmation for procurement).
3) Pen test: we have an internal pentest report from Dec 2026. We can share a redacted PDF, or we can run a vendor engagement and tag Redwood as the requester. If we run a vendor engagement can Redwood accept the vendor’s SOW and SLAs as-is, or do you require changes?
4) Disclosure: 48 hours is OK — can you provide the contact list & preferred format (ticket, email, phone)?

Tentative timeline: procurement needs the SOC AOC + pen test report by next Thurs (7/29) to keep our legal timeline. If Redwood will coordinate a fresh vendor test, we need to lock scope and SOW this week.

Thanks — I’ll wait for the PHI handling confirmation and any SOW notes.

—
Maya Singh
Head of Security & Compliance | BrightPath Health
maya.singh@brightpathhealth.com | +1 (617) 555-4124

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>

Maya — great questions — answering inline below and looping Ben (security engineer) and Laura (ops) for any deeper notes.

> 1) SOC 2 redaction
We can accept a redacted AOC. Please replace customer names with [REDACTED] and keep scope and control descriptions intact. That will satisfy procurement review.

> 2) PHI handling
Redwood supports PHI in our hosted offering under a Business Associate Addendum (BAA). We store customer data in HIPAA-aware regions and offer customer-managed keys for Private deployments. I’m attaching a short summary and the BAA template.

> 3) Pen test options / SOW acceptance
We can accept your internal Dec 2026 report (redacted). If you prefer a fresh vendor test, Redwood can 1) engage Cobalt on BrightPath’s behalf (we have a standard SOW we ask vendors to sign) or 2) BrightPath can commission Cobalt directly and provide the report to Redwood. We typically request the vendor SOW include: scope of assets, authenticated vs unauthenticated tests, testing windows, and a 30-day critical remediation SLA (we can negotiate to 45 if needed). I’ve attached a draft Cobalt SOW (cobalt_sow_draft.pdf) and an internal vulnerability SLA worksheet (redwood_vuln_sla_v1.xlsx) for reference.

> 4) Disclosure contacts / format
Preferred: open a ticket to security@redwood.com and copy your account team. We’ll escalate to on-call for Priority incidents and provide a runbook CSV with required fields. We’ll follow a 48-hour notification expectation.

Proposed next step: Ben, can you join a 30-minute kickoff with BrightPath’s security team tomorrow (Tue 7/20) at 10:00 AM PT to finalize scope and confirm SOW language? If so, I’ll send the invite.
